_meta.description: Verified catalog of in-tree Kubernetes volume plugins removed (or hard-disabled) from the kubelet as part of the CSI-migration effort. Consumed by RemovedVolumePluginCatalog for PluginRemovalAnalyzer (Phase 2 of the Upgrade Breakage Radar). This is the ONLY correct way to catch `gitRepo`-class breakage: the Pod/apps-v1 API schema NEVER drops these fields (GA compatibility guarantee — verified against the real v1.36 bundled schema in Phase 1), but the kubelet-side plugin implementation that actually mounts the volume IS removed at a specific version. Detection = flag the field's PRESENCE in a live workload spec once targetVersion >= removedIn.
_meta.verificationMethod: Every deprecatedIn/removedIn value below was read directly from the official kubernetes/kubernetes CHANGELOG-<version>.md files (raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/master/CHANGELOG/) and/or the current kubernetes.io storage-volumes documentation page, not hand-typed from memory. Exact source URL + matched sentence is recorded per-entry below in `provenance`.
_meta.provisionalNote: photonPersistentDisk is marked provisional — see its own `note` field. All other entries (including the Step-1-added portworxVolume) are confirmed via an explicit, unambiguous CHANGELOG/docs sentence naming the plugin.

step1Addition.description: Backend Step 1 pass added portworxVolume (verified via CHANGELOG-1.25.md, CHANGELOG-1.31.md, CHANGELOG-1.33.md, CHANGELOG-1.36.md — direct whole-file grep, not the summarizer).
step1Addition.kubeadmFlexVolumeAdvisory: The task also asked to consider a 'kubeadm flex-volume removal' (CHANGELOG-1.36.md, PR #136423: 'Removed the integrated support for flex-volumes in kubeadm... mount the directory /usr/libexec/kubernetes/kubelet-plugins/volume/exec in the KCM static pod using kubeadm's extraVolumes mechanism'). This is kubeadm's OWN convenience automation for wiring --flex-volume-plugin-dir into the kube-controller-manager static pod at bootstrap time, NOT a removal of the generic `flexVolume` Pod-spec volume source key (whose kubelet-side mechanism the same quote confirms still works if you mount the directory yourself). It does not map to any detectable field in a live workload spec, so per the task's explicit instruction it is documented here as advisory/out-of-scope rather than forced into a plugins[] row.

plugins.replacement: An initContainer that git-clones the repository into an emptyDir volume shared with the workload container
plugins.remediation: DISABLED BY DEFAULT from 1.33 (GitRepoVolumeDriver gate default false — pods using gitRepo fail on day one of a 1.33 upgrade, three minors before the 1.36 removal; source-verified 2026-08-31). The gitRepo volume plugin was removed. Replace it with an initContainer that git-clones the repository into an emptyDir volume shared with the workload container.
plugins.note: Mechanism nuance: Kubernetes 1.36 locked the gitRepo volume driver to disabled via a feature gate (KEP-5040, kubernetes/kubernetes#136400) 'with no option to turn it back on' -- this is a feature-gate lock, not a literal deletion of the API field (gitRepo remains a valid Pod schema field per the GA compatibility guarantee, confirmed against the real v1.36 bundled schema in Phase 1). It is however functionally equivalent to removal for kubelet behavior: a gitRepo volume can no longer be mounted from 1.36 onward, with no opt-back-in. removedIn=1.36 reflects the version at which it stops functioning, per the official docs.

plugins.note: PROVISIONAL - weaker evidence than the other 8 entries in this catalog. There is no standalone official CHANGELOG sentence naming 'photonPersistentDisk volume plugin removed' (unlike the other 8 plugins here). removedIn=1.16 is INFERRED from directly inspecting the merged code diff for kubernetes/kubernetes PR #72178 ('Remove ovirt/cloudstack/photon cloud providers', merged 2019-06-14, shipped in CHANGELOG-1.16.md), whose file list deletes pkg/volume/photon_pd/{attacher.go,photon_pd.go,photon_util.go,attacher_test.go,photon_pd_test.go} -- i.e. the actual kubelet volume-plugin implementation package. The PR's own title/release-note frame this as removing the PHOTON CLOUD PROVIDER (node/route management), not explicitly the persistent-disk volume plugin, even though the diff shows both were deleted together. deprecatedIn is left null (no dated deprecation announcement specific to the volume plugin was found -- only a 2018-05-10 commit deprecating the cloud provider, a related but distinct subsystem). Corroborating signal (not proof): the current kubernetes.io Volumes doc page has zero mentions of photonPersistentDisk at all (unlike gitRepo/gcePersistentDisk, which get dedicated deprecation-warning sections), consistent with it having been gone a long time. RECOMMENDATION: treat this entry's removedIn as an estimate; do not rely on it alone for a customer upgrade decision without an independent check against the customer's specific current/target version pair.

plugins.remediation: The Portworx in-tree volume plugin was removed in Kubernetes 1.36 (CSIMigrationPortworx, GA/locked since 1.33, has redirected all operations to the pxd.portworx.com CSI driver since then). Ensure the Portworx CSI driver is installed before upgrading to 1.36+; the in-tree plugin no longer functions at all from 1.36 onward.
plugins.note: deprecatedIn=1.25 is the CSIMigrationPortworx feature-gate's Beta promotion (the first per-plugin migration-track signal for Portworx), NOT an explicit 'this plugin is deprecated and will be removed' sentence like cephfs/rbd have — no such standalone sentence was found for Portworx in any changelog searched (1.16-1.37). The migration timeline is fully documented and unambiguous even so: Beta/off-by-default in 1.25 (#110411), Beta/on-by-default in 1.31 (#125016), GA/locked in 1.33 (#129297), and the in-tree plugin fully removed in 1.36 (#135322). removedIn=1.36 is NOT provisional — it has an explicit, unambiguous removal sentence.

plugins.remediation: Migrate cinder volumes to the cinder.csi.openstack.org CSI driver before upgrading to 1.26+. From 1.26 the in-tree plugin is no longer registered by the kubelet, so existing PersistentVolumes fail to mount and StorageClasses naming the in-tree provisioner 'kubernetes.io/cinder' can no longer provision. Install the CSI driver and migrate FIRST — after the upgrade the workloads are already broken.
plugins.note: Removal release established by the kubelet/KCM plugin REGISTRATION, not by directory deletion: `git grep -l 'pkg/volume/cinder"' <tag> -- cmd` matches at v1.25.0 and matches nothing at v1.26.0, so 1.26 is the first release where the in-tree plugin is no longer probed and the volume stops mounting. (Directory presence is NOT a valid signal — pkg/volume/glusterfs outlived its unregistration by a release.) This method reproduces all four pre-existing entries in this catalog exactly: glusterfs 1.26, rbd 1.31, cephfs 1.31, portworxVolume 1.36. deprecatedIn is the release the CSIMigrationOpenStack feature gate reached PreRelease: GA in */features/kube_features.go. In-tree provisioner and replacement driver names are verbatim constants from staging/src/k8s.io/csi-translation-lib/plugins.

plugins.remediation: FlexVolume has been deprecated since Kubernetes 1.23 in favour of CSI. It is still registered as of 1.37, so nothing breaks yet — but kubeadm dropped its support wiring in 1.36 (kube-controller-manager no longer auto-mounts the plugin directory, and the distroless KCM image cannot execute the driver binaries), so a kubeadm cluster on 1.36+ needs --flex-volume-plugin-dir plus extraVolumes and a non-distroless KCM image, or the driver stops working. Plan the move to a CSI driver.
plugins.note: DEPRECATION-ONLY row: removedIn is deliberately null because the plugin is STILL registered at v1.37.0 (`git grep -l 'pkg/volume/flexvolume"' v1.37.0 -- cmd` matches both cmd/kubelet/app/plugins.go and cmd/kube-controller-manager/app/plugins.go). Deprecation release is from CHANGELOG-1.23.md, section 'Deprecation of FlexVolume': 'FlexVolume is deprecated. Out-of-tree CSI driver is the recommended way to write volume drivers in Kubernetes.' The core/v1 Go type carries a matching 'Deprecated: FlexVolume is deprecated' marker, but that comment only shipped in v1.32.0, so it is not the deprecation release.
